style_when: the news is structural and abstract — a stack reordered, a layer added, a flow rerouted — and there is no literal object that carries it, so the idea is stated as a small physical assembly of recognisable parts rather than as bare shapes
prompt: Matte clay 3D render, split-screen diptych with left-right scenario contrast. On the left side, a mechanical compute module integrated with a prominent rotary utility meter and ratcheting gears. On the right side, an identical monolithic server blade block running continuously with heavy heat sinks. Both resting on a weathered brushed steel workbench divided by a strict vertical seam. Matte polymer surfaces with visible moulding seams and deep contact shadows, raking directional light casting long shadows across the divided halves. Muted modern B2B editorial palette, industrial clarity, generous negative space. No text.
negative_prompt: text, letters, words, watermark, labels, garbled typography, people, faces, floating objects
rationale: The story compares two abstract economic models for the same underlying compute. A matte 3D clay render cleanly distills this structural duality into a physical assembly, using a split-screen to contrast the metered module against the dedicated hardware block.
subject: split-screen assembly of a metered server module and a dedicated hardware block
core_thesis: Hosted build minutes and a rented server are the same compute priced two ways, making the decision a pure utilization test of hardware versus engineer upkeep.
core_conflict: Metered per-minute cloud billing versus dedicated rented hardware and its associated human upkeep costs.
composition: split-screen diptych with left-right scenario contrast
